case_analysis.thread_summary: The thread covers a complete Bluetooth SIG qualification support engagement from quotation and planning through registration approval and delivery of compliance documentation. The customer sought guidance on registration requirements, qualification fees, product registration strategy, derivative product handling, and required documentation under the updated qualification process. The consultant managed registration execution, customer review of the submission, SIG approval tracking, and compliance-folder preparation. The registration was successfully approved and the engagement concluded with delivery of compliance records and future product-registration guidance.
case_analysis.key_technical_discussion: A major discussion concerned how products using the same Bluetooth implementation can be added later as derivative products without repeating the initial registration process. The consultant explained the impact of the post-July-2024 qualification environment, including compliance-folder creation and retention obligations under QPRD requirements. The thread also addressed qualification design classification changes caused by the new SIG registration system, resulting in a Multi-Design registration approach rather than the originally expected Single-Design approach. Additional discussion covered TCW usage, review-page validation prior to final submission, and the documentation required to support future SIG audit requests.
case_analysis.key_decision_logic: The consultant consistently based decisions on Bluetooth SIG qualification reuse rules and current registration-system requirements. Products that share the same Bluetooth module and Host stack can be added later through Product List expansion rather than requiring a new qualification. Registration design selection must reflect the actual qualification architecture recognized by the current SIG system, even when newer platform behavior changes the expected registration type. Compliance-folder obligations are driven by qualification policy and must be satisfied regardless of whether additional testing is required.
case_analysis.risk_if_done_wrong: Using an incorrect registration design could result in an invalid qualification path, registration delays, or the need to revise the submission. Failing to maintain the required compliance folder and supporting product documentation could create problems if a Bluetooth SIG audit occurs. Misunderstanding derivative-product eligibility could lead to unnecessary qualification work or unnecessary registration costs for future products. Omitting required review and validation steps before submission could increase the risk of qualification processing issues.
case_analysis.consulting_mistake: The initial quotation assumed a Single-Design registration. After defects in the newly introduced SIG registration site were resolved, the consultant determined that the correct registration type was Multi-Design and updated the quotation and registration approach accordingly. The correction was communicated before qualification execution, preventing the project from proceeding under an incorrect qualification assumption.
case_analysis.consulting_takeaway: Always validate the intended qualification design against the current Bluetooth SIG registration platform before finalizing scope, pricing, or qualification strategy. System-rule changes, qualification-model changes, and registration-platform behavior can affect design classification, reuse eligibility, documentation obligations, and future derivative-product registration options.
